objective: T-20260929-71: run the cheapest negation test (weekly RankIC, two segments, title-shuffle placebo) of whether a short-term rise in Wikipedia page views (VC7_28) predicts next-week SPY-excess returns of current S&P 500 stocks; only if it passes evaluate 4 long / long-short candidates.
target_regime_and_horizon: Weekly horizon (open d+1 to open d+6), S&P 500 constituents, a regime-agnostic attention effect; the recent window from 2024-01-08 is primary and 2016-07 to 2023-12 must show the same sign (survivorship-biased: current members only). Validity window if it ever passes: only while forward IC stays positive; exit signal is 3 months of forward IC below zero.
existing_solution_comparison: `oc research directions check wikipedia pageviews attention` returned dir:wikipedia_pageview_attention_signal (queued, this task) and nothing tested locally. Published record: Moat et al. 2013 (DJIA only, 2004-2012), Wei and Wang 2016 (ML classifiers, 2011-2014; without Wikipedia data the long leg still earns 54.18% vs 57.46%, so the increment is about 3 points and the level looks implausible), Da et al. 2011 (Google SVI predicts 2 weeks of higher prices then reversal). Pyun 2025 (2016-2023 weekly long-short, FF alpha) was read only through a blog summary (SSRN blocked) and no number from it is used. No packaged product or third-party out-of-sample track record for a Wikipedia-attention strategy after 2023 was found; the free API and SIP daily data make the local 2024+ test the missing evidence.
remaining_evidence_gap: No source gave costs, Sharpe or sub-period results for 2024+; the Economics Letters 2024 paper is captcha-blocked (claim_only); the Pyun paper was not opened. Local unknowns: current-constituent survivorship in 2016-2023, article-rename breaks, bot traffic, and whether VC7_28 is only an earnings-week or short-term-reversal proxy.
negative_experiments_checked: Registry: dir:news_attention_features (refuted; news counts/novelty, 0/48 tests pass, gate variants worsened; different data, momentum top-50 gate) and dir:high_freq_news_return_underreaction_drift (refuted, IC -0.005). Neither used Wikipedia views nor a plain S&P 500 cross-section, so this is not a repeat, but the prior is low. Earlier weekly-frequency lessons (capture-ratio metric defect) do not apply because the gate is an IC.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Close-of-UTC-day signal (Wikipedia day d is complete after 20:00 ET), fill at the next session open (lag 0) or one session later (lag 1); weekly hold; 10 bp per side, 20 bp recheck; short leg easy-to-borrow with 0.5%/yr borrow and SPY 252d-beta hedge; prices through sanitize_price_matrices defaults; UTC-day-d views never used with a d close fill.
stop_condition: IC gate (frozen, lag 0 is the gating lag; lag 1 is reported): (a) 2024-01-08-onward weekly RankIC mean > 0 with Newey-West (Bartlett, 4 lags) |t| >= 2.5, (b) 2016-07-to-2023-12 IC mean has the same sign (>0), (c) the real 2024-onward IC exceeds the 95th percentile of 500 title-shuffle placebo ICs. Each statistic is the median across the five weekday rebalance offsets. Any failure -> refuted, no ledger, no candidates.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Fetch about 500 per-article daily view series (free, single thread), compute weekly RankIC of VC7_28 vs next-week SPY-excess open-to-open returns at lag 0 and 1 over both segments with Newey-West t, plus 500 title-shuffle placebos and the drop list; no portfolio ledger.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: 2024-01-08-onward median-offset IC > 0 with |t| >= 2.5, 2016-07 to 2023-12 IC same sign, and real 2024+ IC above the 95th placebo percentile, all at lag 0.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Any of the three fails at lag 0: refuted, close the registry row, build no ledger and add no variants.

sources.claim: Data on changes in how often financially related Wikipedia pages were viewed may have contained early signs of stock market moves.
sources.market_and_period: DJIA-30 constituents and related financial-topic pages, weekly, 2004-2012 (per the prior registry row)
sources.applicability: Foundational weekly-pageview-change design (Moat, Preis et al.) that the VC7_28 signal descends from; establishes that weekly changes, not levels, are the object.
sources.limitations: Small DJIA universe, pre-2013, no realistic costs or shorting frictions in the abstract; the trading rule is tested on the index, not on constituents cross-sectionally.

sources.claim: An increase in SVI predicts higher stock prices in the next 2 weeks and an eventual price reversal within the year.
sources.market_and_period: Russell 3000 stocks, Google search volume index, 2004-2008
sources.applicability: Closest peer-reviewed cross-sectional attention result: a positive 1-2 week drift then reversal. Motivates a weekly horizon and warns that a longer holding period would give the sign back.
sources.limitations: Google SVI, not Wikipedia; 2004-2008 sample; retail-attention channel that may have weakened after 2010; no transaction costs in the abstract.

sources.claim: If we exclude Wikipedia data from the classifiers, the return of the long position shrinks to 54.18% per annum, both economically and statistically significant.
sources.market_and_period: All NYSE and NASDAQ stocks, 2011-2014, machine-learning classifiers on Wikipedia views plus price features
sources.applicability: Cross-sectional Wikipedia page-view evidence on individual stocks. The same passage shows the classifier earns 54.18% without Wikipedia data, so the Wikipedia increment is small; the headline 57.46% and 65.27% figures are not used as targets.
sources.limitations: Machine-learned classifiers, 2011-2014 only, unrealistic returns (over 50% per annum) that suggest look-ahead or no costs; the increment attributable to Wikipedia is about 3 percentage points.

sources.claim: Wiki-visits spike at key informational events such as earnings announcements.
sources.applicability: Shows page views on S&P 500 company articles are event-driven (earnings) and reflect information acquisition, so VC7_28 mostly re-encodes earnings weeks; the test must be read next to the earnings-drift family already run.
sources.limitations: Studies determinants and price discovery at earnings announcements, not return prediction across weeks; no trading rule or costs.

sources.claim: Our backtest yields a performance of about 17bps per week which only weakly depends on the kind of data on which predictors are based, i.e. either past price returns or Google Trends data, or both.
sources.market_and_period: Google Trends keywords and US index/stocks, 2004-2011-era backtest
sources.applicability: Negative-evidence source: shows that search-attention predictability is mostly the price-return predictability and that keyword selection is the main bias. This is why our test fixes titles before looking at any return and adds a title-shuffle placebo.
sources.limitations: Google Trends not Wikipedia; keyword-selected indices, not S&P 500 constituents; 2014 preprint.

sources.claim: A long-short trading strategy based on Wikipedia page view changes outperforms the market and delivers positive abnormal returns.
sources.market_and_period: NYSE and Nasdaq firms, 2016-2023, Quiver Quantitative page-view data (per secondary summary of SSRN 5172055)
sources.applicability: The only source motivating a weekly long-short on page-view changes in 2016-2023. Read only through a blog summary (SSRN blocked), so no number from the paper is used in any threshold.
sources.limitations: Secondary summary; no Sharpe, cost, or sub-period figures; the paper itself was not opened (claim_only).

sources.claim: The public pageviews dataset has per-article and per-project view counts for all Wikimedia Foundation projects since May 2015 and filters out as many spiders and bots as can be detected.
sources.market_and_period: All Wikimedia projects, from May 2015; agent-type user filtering of spiders and bots
sources.applicability: Defines the data: per-article daily counts from 2015-05 on, so 2016-07 onward is fully available; the fetch uses the agent type user to exclude detected spiders.
sources.limitations: Bot filtering is heuristic ('as many spiders and bots as we can detect'); automated traffic can still contaminate individual articles.

sources.claim: The constituents table of the List of S&P 500 companies carries the ticker symbol, the company article link, GICS sector and date added for each current member.
sources.market_and_period: Current S&P 500 members as of 2026-09-29 (survivorship-biased for 2016-2023)
sources.applicability: Source of the ticker to article-title map; because only current members are listed, 2016-2023 results carry survivorship bias and the 2024-onward segment is the primary evidence.
sources.limitations: Current constituents only; article titles for renamed companies can break history; redirects are resolved by the API but ambiguous titles (e.g. FDXF, KEY) are kept and reported.
